# Native Pinocchio Torque Replay

## Calculation and Admission

F06c #11900 extends the independent replay boundary to actual Pinocchio ABA
through the existing public `PinocchioPhysicsEngine.step(..., integrator="rk4")`.
It does not introduce another integrator or replay schema. Tools T01 supplies
`ExperimentReplayBundle`; shared native admission checks its serialization,
capabilities, fixed input grid, terminal sentinel and post-limit efforts.

For this unconstrained policy the equations are
\(\dot q=\mathcal{N}(q)v\),
\(M(q)\dot v+h(q,v)=B u\).
Each declared unit SimpleTransmission maps one ordered motor torque in N m
to one native revolute tangent coordinate. Floating-base generalized forces
remain zero. The adapter reads back the engine's effective `tau` before
stepping. Pinocchio has generalized forces rather than a native motor object;
the explicit source-declared unit mapping is part of this adapter's policy.

Only fixed, floating and bounded revolute URDF joints are admitted. Motors
need unique identities and finite positive native effort limits. Unsupported
source tags, collision, mimic, damping/actuator extensions, external resources
and nonunit reductions fail admission. Joint limit forces are not implemented
by this policy; geometric feasibility remains a separate acceptance gate.

## Complete State and Integration

Physical state is complete native configuration and tangent velocity at time
zero. The original fixture has `nq=8`, `nv=7`, including a floating quaternion.
Inputs and state must be finite; configuration normalization must already hold
within `1e-12`. No normalization, equilibrium operation or per-frame reset
repairs an invalid state. Native Data quantities and the acceleration cache are
derived from q/v and current torque; fresh execution recomputes them.

The existing engine holds torque during its four ABA evaluations and uses
`pin.integrate` for each configuration update. The adapter records this exact
implementation, not a newly asserted global fourth-order Lie-group method.
Every interval is fixed-duration zero-order hold. The last saved row equals
the preceding row and is a sentinel, never executed. Replay receives no
observation or controller and uses one fresh owned native engine continuously.

## Provenance and Numerical Evidence

Source URDF bytes, native `Model.saveToString()` output, ordered channels,
complete state schema, stepping/input policy and loaded Pinocchio version are
bound. Provider identity hashes the native Python extension, existing engine,
adapter and shared admission source. This is not a transitive-library closure
attestation; callers require exclusive process ownership and no monkeypatches.

Commit `f273e45f2f` records missing-module RED tests before implementation.
Twelve actual Pinocchio4.1.0 checks pass in Python3.12.14, including saturated
closed-loop-to-open-loop reproduction with `1e-12` absolute q/v tolerance,
native input scattering, model replacement and invalid state/input/source
rejection. A 0.256-second synthetic constant-input probe compares 16, 8 and
4 ms steps with a separately integrated 1 ms reference. Terminal error uses
native `pin.difference` plus velocity norm and decreases under refinement.
This establishes fixture-specific convergence, not full-swing accuracy.

## Reproduction and Remaining Gates

Use an isolated copy of `test_native_pinocchio_torque_replay.py` to avoid
optional-provider mocks in the repository conftest. Set `PYTHONPATH` to the
production repository plus pinned Tools `src` and `src/shared/python`, disable
pytest plugin autoload and use one OMP/BLAS/MKL numerical worker. Execute with
the actual native provider and retain its JUnit/run receipts. Provider skips
do not qualify physics.

Native contact/grip constraints, all production variants, capture-specific
anatomy, muscular actuation, independently heldout prediction and all-model
six-engine parity remain unqualified. Primitive replay is an execution
prerequisite. It does not close the parent F06 or the full matching epic.
